metadata.note: Albany, GA's historic rail connection: the South Western Railroad, a Central of Georgia-affiliated line running Macon-Americus-Albany through the state's southwest cotton belt. The South Western reached Americus from Macon around 1854, transforming it from a small courthouse town into a regional trade hub. It then bought a partially-built Americus-Albany line from the Georgia and Florida Railroad in 1857 and pushed it to completion that year -- the South Western and the Georgia and Florida were formally consolidated Dec 19 1859. Geometry is a real-town waypoint approximation (Macon-Americus-Albany), straight-line segments between documented stations -- NOT digitized from period track maps. EXPANDED 2026-08-23: the Macon-Americus-Albany geometry was upgraded from a 2-3 point straight-line approximation to real-traced OpenStreetMap track geometry (traced length 172.9 km / 107.4 mi, matching the sourced ~104 mi closely). Three real-traced branches added: Fort Valley-Columbus (the South Western's actual FIRST connection, 1853, via the separate Muscogee Railroad), and Smithville-Cuthbert-Eufaula, AL / Cuthbert-Fort Gaines (both 1860) -- confirming the system did reach into Alabama, at Eufaula. All three branches' traced lengths matched their sourced mileages within a mile or two, corroborating the routing.
sources: https://www.cofga.org/railway/history/the-south-western-railroad-company/ (South Western reached Americus from Macon c.1854; bought the partially-built Georgia and Florida Railroad's Americus-Albany line in 1857 and completed it; consolidated with the Georgia and Florida Dec 19 1859)
https://railfanning.org/trackside/americus/ (South Western's arrival transformed Americus from a courthouse town into a regional trade center)
metadata.not_yet_sourced: Exact month/day rail traffic began running Americus-Albany in 1857 (only the year is sourced); precise frequency for any era, all estimated; exact discontinuation date for through Macon-Albany passenger service (approximated here at Amtrak's May 1 1971 creation, since this specific route was not among those Amtrak continued, but not directly confirmed -- the well-documented Central of Georgia 'Nancy Hanks' train that also ended right before Amtrak ran a different route, Atlanta-Savannah, not this one).
metadata.line_label_audit: 2026-08-24: line labels normalised repo-wide to "<operating company>: <line name>" -- the company's common display name (legal suffixes dropped), then the line as a passenger would have known it, or its two terminals where the line carried no advertised name. Long intermediate station lists were reduced to endpoints. For features spanning several operators the company shown is the one that ran the line for most of its drawn years. See CLAUDE.md Rule 6.

segments.note: The South Western's first major connection, predating even its own Macon-Americus segment's completion: investment to reach Fort Valley began 1851, track reached the Flint River by 1852, and Columbus got its rail connection to Macon and the sea in June 1853 via the separate Muscogee Railroad (whose eastern end at Butler the South Western completed after Muscogee faltered in 1853); Muscogee formally consolidated into the South Western in 1856. Frequency estimated, unsourced; discontinuation approximated at Amtrak's 1971 creation, not directly confirmed

segments.note: The South Western built a branch from Smithville (on the Macon-Albany main line) west through Cuthbert, splitting three miles beyond it -- one leg continuing to Eufaula, Alabama, the other southwest to Fort Gaines (see companion feature) -- both completed 1860, giving the South Western its only crossing into Alabama. Frequency estimated, unsourced; discontinuation approximated at Amtrak's 1971 creation, not directly confirmed
